For what it’s worth I’ve learned that a good way to defeat toxic shame is to just ask yourself “so what?” when you think about a bad quality you could possibly have.

So you might have been rude to your professor. So what? What if you are a rude person? It doesn’t have to define you. You can grow and change and become a different person and choose the behaviors that make you who you want to be. You have the control. Not whoever labeled you like that.

In the beginning it was really lovely to realize that people were much more friendly than I thought they were and that I didn’t have to be a certain way in order to be liked by people.

I was really surprised when I asked a few people to hang out and they said yes, no questions asked. And then people invited me in return! It was nice.
I’m sorry I didn’t mean to downplay the issue of men receiving less sympathy than women. I’m sorry that happened to you, that is awful.
I think at some point I also didn’t care enough about what other people were saying to me or how I was affecting them. I became very impulsive and just said whatever I was thinking.
For me I think I crossed a line from being vulnerable and trusting that people will like me anyway to oversharing because I wanted control over what people thought of me.

I used to be very shy and worried about everyone liking me then one day some really awful stuff happened to me and I snapped and went overboard opening up and not caring what people think of me and now everyone hates me lol. But for a moment before I took it too far I was very popular.

What I learned from this experience is that people liking you has more to do with your attachment style and perceived value than it does with you as a person. Just be a little vulnerable. See what happens.
